knowledge.text: Jointly adding an 'observed-without-goal = exhausted' rewording of the exploration principle plus a single-pass Search Strategy section (no immediate return to a just-observed location; no restart of a completed numbered sequence while another untried location remains; open closed containers before judging them empty) did not uniformly reduce repeated sweeps. On 'put a cellphone in shelf' (train:0005), 'put some newspaper on sofa' (train:0006) and 'put a pencil in desk' (train:0007) the Candidate executed more actions than its verified Parent counterpart (44 vs 30; 50 vs 41; 14 vs 10) and re-entered drawer sequences it had already observed empty (Q6:14, Q6:23, Q6:32; Q8:7, Q8:9), although the Parent also revisited observed-empty drawers (P6:8); all six sides still succeeded. Across the batch no pair regressed from Parent-success to Candidate-failure and action counts were equal in five pairs. The joint guidance was therefore not uniformly adhered to, and its intended cycling reduction is not established from these pairs; the principle rewording and the Search Strategy section are not separable from each other here.

On 'look at statue under the desklamp' (train:0004) the Candidate completed the task in 3 actions versus the Parent's 27: the Parent swept shelves 1-9, then opened drawers 1-3, then restarted the shelf sequence (P5:16) before reaching dresser 1 (P5:25), took the statue (P5:26) and used the desklamp (P5:27), whereas the Candidate went directly to dresser 1 (Q5:1), took the statue (Q5:2) and used the desklamp there (Q5:3). This is a large material asymmetry consistent with the edit's discouragement of restarting a completed numbered sweep, but the Candidate's initial choice of dresser 1 is not uniquely determined by the guidance (which constrains revisits rather than which location type to try first), so the whole reduction cannot be attributed to the edit; both sides succeeded.

Where the Parent already followed a direct route, the added search guidance produced no observed detour or container-handling regression: on 'put a soapbar in garbagecan' and 'put some statue on coffeetable' the Parent and Candidate used identical action sequences and equal action counts (4 vs 4; 16 vs 16), including opening closed drawers before judging them empty in train:0009 (P10:2, Q10:2), and all succeeded.

Under the current edit's 'Acquisition Search' section — which, once a numbered container class is being swept, directs continuing to further instances of that same class (preferring higher-numbered ones) before switching to another class or an open surface — current Candidate runs stayed inside one large container class for most of the episode and never selected surface candidates that held the target: on train:0016 ('clean some knife and put it in drawer') the Candidate worked through cabinets 1-20 (Q7:1-Q7:39) and never selected countertop 1, where the Parent took knife 1 (P7:1, P7:2) and finished in 7 steps, ending at the 50-step limit; on train:0017 ('clean some lettuce and put it in diningtable') it swept cabinets 1-13, re-swept them, then cycled among cabinet 12/13, fridge 1 and countertop 1 (Q8:31-Q8:50) and never selected diningtable 1, where the Parent took lettuce 1 (P8:33, P8:34) and finished in 38, ending at the step limit; on train:0019 ('clean some plate and put it in fridge') it swept cabinets 1-11 and took plate 2 from cabinet 11 (Q10:22), though countertop 1 held a plate the Parent took immediately (P10:1, P10:2), succeeding in 27 vs 7. These two Parent-success/Candidate-failure regressions and one large step inflation are consistent with the class-priority widening container search while unvisited surfaces holding the target were never tried. Limit: the clause constrains staying inside a class already started, not which class or surface to start from, so these whole-task differences are consistent with, but not uniquely attributable to, the clause.

The current edit's anti-revisit clause ('do not choose either of the last two locations you visited when the target was not observed there'; do not alternate between the same two recently checked locations; keep broadening to new containers/classes/surfaces) did not remove the short revisit cycles the runs show, because a cycle of three or more sites satisfies the literal 'last two' restriction while still returning to recently checked instances: on train:0013 the Candidate repeated cabinets 13, 11, 12, 10 from about Q4:21 to Q4:50 (both sides terminating at the 50-step limit without finding the dishsponge); on train:0015 it repeated cabinets 6, 7, 8, 9 across Q6:17-Q6:29; on train:0017 it repeated fridge 1, countertop 1, cabinet 12, cabinet 13 across Q8:44-Q8:50; and on train:0014 it traversed shelves 1-4 three times (Q5:1-Q5:12), taking 20 actions to the Parent's 12 while both succeeded. The un-edited Parent also revisited locations in some runs (e.g., P5:6 returned to shelf 1 after checking shelves 1-4), so no uniform anti-revisit contrast is established. Limit: the Actor sees only the current observation, the admissible actions and the last two pre-action observation/action pairs and keeps no persistent notes, so whether the clause was ignored or simply insufficient for tracking older checked locations cannot be separated.

Where the required object was reached without a prolonged search, the added Acquisition Search section produced no observed change and no regression in current pairs: on train:0010 (toiletpaper to toiletpaperhanger, 8 steps), train:0011 (toiletpaper to toiletpaperhanger, 7), train:0012 (clean apple to diningtable, 10) and train:0018 (clean lettuce to fridge, 7) the Parent and Candidate action sequences were identical and both sides succeeded.

The one current pair in which the Candidate succeeded while the Parent did not — train:0015 'put a clean kettle in cabinet' (Parent terminated at the 50-step limit, Candidate succeeded in 43) — does not isolate a benefit of the added section: the Candidate still swept cabinets 1-9 and repeated cabinets 6-9 (Q6:17-Q6:29) and opened drawers 1-4 (Q6:31, Q6:37) before taking kettle 2 from stoveburner 6 (Q6:39) — an appliance outside the swept classes — and cleaning and placing it (Q6:41, Q6:43), while the Parent never reached that appliance. The whole-task difference therefore cannot be attributed to the class-sweep or anti-revisit clauses.
